subject: Meteorology
title: Stratocumulus Clouds
description: Learn Stratocumulus Clouds in one minute.

hook.text: Stratocumulus clouds are the most common cloud type on Earth, covering about 20% of the planet at any time.

buildup.text: They form as lumpy, rolling sheets—like stratus with some vertical texture and breaks of blue sky.

discovery.text: They appear when weak convection stirs a stable layer—enough to create lumps, not enough for tall clouds.

twist.text: Over cold ocean currents, stratocumulus can persist for weeks—reflecting sunlight and cooling the surface.

climax.text: Climate models struggle with stratocumulus—small errors in simulating them cause huge swings in projections.

punchline.text: The most common cloud is also the most underrated.

quiz.question: What percentage of Earth does stratocumulus cover at any given time?
